skill.name: hermesemailskill
skill.description: Use when Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Claude Code, Cowork, or another AI agent needs to plan, review, implement, audit, or improve email work focused on fast delivery decisions, message QA, launch coordination, and concise status handoffs. Triggers include requests about preflight checklists, launch-room summaries, transactional copy reviews, escalation notes, and send readiness calls.
skill.summary: Plan, QA, and coordinate email launches with clear send readiness decisions and approval gates.
skill.author: Sequenzy

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns across the three prompt-only files. Manual review found no prompt injection attempts, data exfiltration intent, executable code, network behavior, or requests to bypass approval gates.

content.value_statement: Email launches can fail when teams miss audience, copy, link, or approval risks. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce fast QA checks, launch summaries, and approval-ready handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Creates launch readiness summaries using ready, caveated, blocked, or needs review decisions.
Builds compressed preflight checks for copy, links, rendering, segments, sender identity, and tracking.
Reviews transactional and lifecycle email copy for subject, CTA, and promise consistency.
Drafts incident timelines with observed behavior, suspected cause, blast radius, mitigation, and owner.
Separates analysis from live email actions and requires explicit approval for high-risk changes.
limitations: Does not send email, import contacts, edit DNS, or change production automation by itself.
Requires accurate campaign details, test sends, segment rules, and provider status to make useful recommendations.
Does not replace legal, compliance, deliverability, or brand approval for regulated sends.
Cannot verify live rendering or delivery behavior without supplied evidence from tools or providers.

use_cases.title: Preflight a Marketing Send
use_cases.description: Check audience, exclusions, copy, links, sender identity, tracking, and approval status before launch.

use_cases.title: Review Transactional Copy
use_cases.description: Compare the message promise, subject line, CTA, merge tags, and fallback values before deployment.

use_cases.title: Summarize an Email Incident
use_cases.description: Create a concise timeline, blast radius, mitigation status, next owner, and monitoring plan.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Send Readiness Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hermesemailskill to review this email send brief. Tell me if it is ready, blocked, or needs review. Include copy, links, audience, exclusions, sender identity, tracking, and approval checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a clear go or no-go review before an email launch.

prompt_templates.title: Transactional Message QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hermesemailskill to audit this transactional email. Check whether the subject, CTA, body copy, merge tags, fallback values, footer, and user promise are consistent.
prompt_templates.scenario: A product team is preparing a transactional or lifecycle message.

prompt_templates.title: Launch Room Status Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hermesemailskill to turn these notes into a launch-room handoff. Separate blockers, caveats, owner actions, approval status, deadline, and post-send monitoring.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a concise status summary during a time-sensitive launch.

prompt_templates.title: Incident Timeline and Mitigation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use $hermesemailskill to analyze this email incident evidence. Build a timeline, identify suspected causes, estimate blast radius, name mitigation options, and list approval gates before live changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user is coordinating a live email incident response.

output_examples.input: Review a campaign brief with final copy, test-send links, audience count, exclusions, and launch deadline.
output_examples.output: A readiness summary that marks the send as ready with caveats, lists two link checks, confirms exclusions, and names the approval owner.

output_examples.input: Audit a password reset email before deployment.
output_examples.output: A copy review that compares the subject, CTA, fallback text, footer, and user promise, then flags missing merge-tag evidence.

output_examples.input: Summarize notes from a delayed promotional send incident.
output_examples.output: An incident timeline with observed behavior, likely cause, affected audience, current mitigation, next owner, and monitoring window.

best_practices: Provide the full send brief, audience rules, exclusions, test links, deadline, and approval chain.
Ask for a decision summary that separates blockers from polish issues.
Keep live sends, imports, DNS changes, and suppression edits behind explicit human approval.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to approve a live send without test evidence and an approval owner.
Do not treat draft copy feedback as compliance, legal, or deliverability clearance.
Do not combine incident diagnosis with live production changes in one unapproved step.

faq.question: Can this skill send emails?
faq.answer: No. It prepares analysis, QA notes, and handoffs. Live send actions require explicit human approval outside the skill.

faq.question: What inputs improve the review?
faq.answer: Provide the brief, audience size, segment rules, exclusions, copy, test send, links, provider status, deadline, and approval chain.

faq.question: Does it support transactional emails?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review transactional and lifecycle messages for promise, CTA, subject, fallback values, and footer consistency.

faq.question: Can it help during an incident?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize observed behavior, suspected cause, blast radius, mitigation, next owner, and monitoring notes.

faq.question: Is it useful for nontechnical teams?
faq.answer: Yes. The outputs use decision language such as ready, blocked, ready with caveats, or needs review.

faq.question: Does it replace approval workflows?
faq.answer: No. It makes approval status explicit and keeps high-risk live-system actions behind human confirmation.
